correctness.rationale: For a directed simple cycle, the only non-backtracking simple directed circuits are the two oriented Hamiltonian cycles. If neither survives, SCCs are precisely the connected components of fully bidirectional edges. Two disjoint orientation sets yield the exact squared two-point probability, and the one-deficient-edge complement event yields the exact full-connectivity polynomial. In the critical regime independent missing-orientation Bernoulli point processes converge to independent Poisson point processes, with double marks vanishing; conditioned on both colours, normalized cyclic gaps give sorted finite Dirichlet spacings and convergence in ℓ¹. In the n(1-p)->infinity, p->1 regime the longest-run event count has convergent factorial moments since starts within k are mutually exclusive and distant starts independent, establishing Gumbel asymptotics. Code exhausts all 5,440 configurations for n=3..6 and checks rational identities; 5,482 assertions passed. Finite tests are not used in place of the infinite proof.

Its Lemma 1.2 couples to fully bidirectional bonds, but neither it nor the compared primary works states the finite-ring all-SCC trichotomy: exact two-point and full strong probabilities, two-colour Poisson circular spacings with Hamiltonian-tour atom, and rare-cut Gumbel extreme. value.rationale: The newly introduced bidirected percolation model has a natural finite-volume question: the entire strongly connected partition on a cycle when missing arcs are rare. A single surviving oriented Hamiltonian tour produces a macroscopic atom absent from standard undirected 1D percolation; if both tours fail, the remaining cuts form a Poisson/finite-Dirichlet partition. The crossover law gives joint sizes rather than a routine isolated probability, and its Gumbel boundary identifies the contrasting microscopic extreme scale. Such complete phase information is a substantial structural classification within the natural graph geometry, with clear interpretation as robust bidirectional communication under independent one-way failures.
